title: Hidden Edge 3
content:
Lan Xichen stumbled back several steps, barely keeping his footing, his mind entirely blank in the face of what had just unfolded.

Across the room, Lan Wangji brought his palm down against the back of the elegant Guanyin statue. The stone form shuddered, ripped from its plinth, and hurtled straight toward the trench. Nie Mingjue was still glaring down at the twisted corpse dangling in his grip when the massive stone deity slammed into him like a flying mountain, violently pinning him back into the coffin.

Wei Wuxian vaulted onto the rim, planting his boots firmly on the statue’s chest. The wooden lid had been blown into splinters; using the goddess herself as a makeshift seal was their only play. Down below, Nie Mingjue pounded relentlessly against the stone underside, trying to smash his way out. The concussive shocks rattled right through the statue, throwing Wei Wuxian off balance and nearly flipping him off. Staggering to stay upright, he realized there was no way he could hold his balance long enough to draw a single talisman.

"Lan Zhan! Quick, get up here with me!" he shouted. "We need more weight—two more punches and this statue’s gonna split right in half—"

Before the words had fully cleared his mouth, the world tilted sideways. Lan Wangji had gripped one edge of the coffin and hoisted the end clean off the ground.

That was to say: with only his left hand, he was holding up a solid hardwood coffin, two full-grown corpses inside it, an entire stone statue of Guanyin, and Wei Wuxian perched on top of it—all of it tilted on one end, hovering off the floorboards.

Wei Wuxian’s jaw dropped.

He’d always known Lan Wangji had monstrous arm strength, but this... this was absurd.

Lan Wangji didn’t so much as blink. Flicking his right wrist, he sent a silver guqin string flying. It moved like a lightning-fast weaver's shuttle, whipping around the coffin and the stone statue dozens of times to lash them together in an iron embrace. Then came a second string, and a third. Only when he was dead certain that Nie Mingjue and Jin Guangyao were sealed down so tight they couldn't twitch did he abruptly let go with his left hand.

The base of the coffin hit the flagstones with a deafening crash. Wei Wuxian lurched forward, but Lan Wangji stepped right into his path, catching him clean against his chest and setting him gently on his feet. The very same hand that had just deadlifted a small mountain held Wei Wuxian with feather-light care.

Lan Xichen stood transfixed, staring blankly at the casket wound tight in seven shimmering guqin strings, completely hollowed out. Nie Huaisang reached over, waving a timid hand in front of his face.

"X-Xichen-ge... you alright?"

Lan Xichen turned a dazed look toward him. "Huaisang... just now. Did he really try to sneak an attack on me from behind?"

"I... I think that's what I saw..."

Hearing the hesitation, Lan Xichen’s voice edged with raw desperation. "Think carefully. Are you certain?"

"When you put it like that, I'm not sure anymore..." Nie Huaisang shrank back. "It just... it really looked like it..."

"Don't give me 'looked like'!" Lan Xichen snapped, his composure fraying. "Did he or did he not?!"

Cornered, Nie Huaisang looked close to tears. "I don't know! I really don't know!"

Whenever he was backed into a corner, this was the only line he ever had. Lan Xichen buried his face in his hands, nursing a skull-splitting migraine, drained of the will to speak.

From across the room, Wei Wuxian piped up: "Huaisang-xiong."

Nie Huaisang blinked. "Huh?"

"How did Su She manage to stab you earlier?"

"He was trying to make a run for it with San-ge—I mean, Sect Leader Jin—on his back," Nie Huaisang said, rubbing his thigh. "I got in his way, so..."

"Really?" Wei Wuxian smiled faintly. "Funny. If I remember right, where you were standing wasn't anywhere near their escape route."

"Come on," Nie Huaisang blurted out defensively. "You think I threw myself onto his blade on purpose just to get stabbed?!"

Wei Wuxian gave a mild smile. "Never said that."

"Then what are you getting at, Wei-xiong?"

"Just connecting a few dots."

"What dots?"

"Jin Guangyao claimed someone sent him a blackmail letter," Wei Wuxian said casually, "promising to drag every single one of his secrets into the light after seven days, giving him the choice to either slit his own throat or wait for his executioner. Assuming he wasn't spinning lies, that letter was an entirely pointless move."

He looked at Nie Huaisang. "If you actually want to expose someone's dirty laundry, you just drop the evidence on the world. Why go out of your way to tip off the culprit that you’ve got them dead to rights?"

"Didn't San-ge—Sect Leader Jin—say they wanted him to commit suicide to atone?"

"Come on," Wei Wuxian snorted. "Anyone with half a brain knows Jin Guangyao would never roll over and kill himself. What was the point? It seems completely useless on paper. But someone capable of digging up secrets that deeply buried doesn't play a garbage move for fun. A redundant step like that always has an angle. It was meant to trigger a reaction—to cultivate something specific."

Lan Xichen looked up, his voice hollow. "Cultivate what?"

Lan Wangji’s voice was like cold iron: "Murderous intent."

On any other day, Zewu-jun would have seen through it in a heartbeat, but his mind had been torn to shreds tonight.

"Spot on," Wei Wuxian continued. "That letter pushed Jin Guangyao’s murderous streak to a fever pitch. If he was told his days were numbered, his only instinct was to strike first—trap the main forces of the prominent clans at the Burial Mounds and butcher them all in one fell swoop, leaving no one left to bury him"

Lan Xichen frowned. "You're saying that was the sender's goal all along? To bait him into slaughtering everyone?"

"That's my guess."

Lan Xichen shook his head, baffled. "Then what was this person after? Exposing Jin Guangyao, or drowning the sects in blood?"

"Look at what happened when the siege failed," Wei Wuxian said simply. "The moment the clans retreated to Lotus Pier, boiling with fury and paranoia, Bicao and Sisi showed up right on cue. I don't buy for a second that their timing was an accident. Every revelation hit all at once, detonating like gunpowder."

He paused, letting his gaze settle heavily on the room. "The mastermind didn't just want Jin Guangyao ruined. They wanted the entire world to turn on him with feral bloodlust. A single, lethal blow—one that left him zero room to wiggle out."

Nie Huaisang let out a low whistle. "Sounds like whoever did this has been setting up the board for a very long time."

Wei Wuxian eyed him. "Speaking of which, wasn't Chifeng-zun’s body under your care, Sect Leader Nie?"

"It was," Nie Huaisang stammered. "But I just got word tonight that my brother’s remains vanished from Qinghe! That's why I was rushing back in the first place, only to get snatched up by Su She on the road..."

"Sect Leader Nie, you visit Gusu Lan and Lanling Jin quite often, don't you?"

"I mean, yeah."

"Then do you really not know Mo Xuanyu?"

Nie Huaisang blinked innocently. "What?"

"I remember running into you right after the sacrificial ritual," Wei Wuxian said, watching his eyes. "You acted like you’d never laid eyes on me, even asking Hanguang-jun who I was. Back in the day, Mo Xuanyu pestered Jin Guangyao relentlessly, even getting his hands on his private collection of secret manuscripts. Meanwhile, you were always running to Sect Leader Jin to cry on his shoulder. Even if you two weren't close, you’re telling me you never crossed paths with him once?"

Nie Huaisang ruffled his messy hair, looking embarrassed. "Wei-xiong, Koi Tower is massive. I can't possibly meet every single person there, and even if I did, I wouldn't remember them all. Besides..." He lowered his voice awkwardly. "You know what Mo Xuanyu's reputation was like. It was... scandalous. The Lanling Jin Clan kept him locked out of sight as much as possible. It’s totally normal that I never met him. Xichen-ge probably never met him either."

"Fair point," Wei Wuxian conceded breezily. "Zewu-jun didn't know him either."

"Right?!" Nie Huaisang threw his hands up. "And I don't get it—even if I had met him, why would I pretend not to? What would be the point?"

Wei Wuxian chuckled softly. "Nothing. Just struck me as odd, that's all."

The point, Wei Wuxian thought privately, would be to figure out whether the shell called 'Mo Xuanyu' was still the original coward, or the vengeful ghost he’d paid for.

How could the timid, sniveling Mo Xuanyu described by everyone have ever had the guts to slice his own soul to pieces for a sacrificial summon?

Why had Chifeng-zun’s left arm suddenly been tossed out into the open? Could Jin Guangyao really have been careless enough to let it slip from his vaults?

And why did it happen to manifest at the Mo Estate of all places, landing right in the lap of the newly reborn Wei Wuxian, rather than turning up anywhere else in the world?

Chifeng-zun’s burial had been handled by the Qinghe Nie Sect from start to finish. Had Nie Huaisang—a brother who practically worshiped Chifeng-zun—truly stayed oblivious for over a decade that the corpse in the tomb was a fake?

Wei Wuxian was far more inclined to believe another scenario entirely.

Perhaps before Nie Mingjue died, Nie Huaisang really had been the clueless "Head-Shaker" who knew nothing. But after his brother’s death, he figured out everything. He learned that Nie Mingjue’s corpse had been swapped out, and he saw the monstrous face behind the gentle mask of his sworn third brother.

He had spent years trying to dig up his brother's missing remains, moving heaven and earth only to secure a single severed left arm.

That was where he’d hit a brick wall. No more clues, no more leads. On top of that, the severed arm was a feral, bloodthirsty calamity that he had zero ability to tame; keeping it close was a death sentence waiting to happen. So, his mind went to the one person alive—or dead—who made a career out of taming untamable horrors.

The Yiling Laozu.

Except the Yiling Laozu had been torn to shreds thirteen years ago. How do you bring back a pile of ash?

That was when he thought of another convenient pawn: Mo Xuanyu, recently kicked down the steps of Koi Tower.

Perhaps Nie Huaisang had struck up conversations with the disgraced youth, fishing for secrets, and learned that the miserable outcast had stumbled across an ancient, forbidden text in Jin Guangyao’s private vault—a ritual that traded a living soul to summon a vengeful spirit. He merely had to plant the seed in the ear of a desperate, abused young man pushed to the brink of madness.

And what vengeful spirit to summon?

The Yiling Laozu, of course.

Broken by abuse, Mo Xuanyu finally drew the circle in his own blood. And Nie Huaisang seized that exact window to toss out the scalding hot potato he could no longer manage alone: Chifeng-zun’s left arm.

From that moment on, the plan ran on autopilot. He didn't have to lift a finger or risk his neck hunting down the rest of Nie Mingjue's body; he offloaded every single dangerous, exhausting lead onto Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji. All he had to do was sit back and watch the show.

Take that bizarre string of cat mutilations that Jin Ling, Lan Sizhui, and the other juniors had stumbled across—that had clearly been staged to draw them in. Add in that fictional "hunter" who gave them directions in the nearby woods, and the play was obvious: herd a pack of sheltered noble brats straight into the horrors of Yi City. If Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji had slipped up for even a second and failed to protect them, any blood spilled in Yi City would have been slapped onto Jin Guangyao's tab today anyway.

The more dirt they could pile onto Jin Guangyao, the better. The more mistakes they could bait the cautious fox into making, the more leverage they held. Anything to make his final drop into hell as gruesome as humanly possible.

Lan Wangji nudged the overturned black trunk beside the coffin with the tip of Bichen, glancing at the binding runes carved into the iron. Turning to Wei Wuxian, he murmured:

"The head."

This coffer had likely been used to store Nie Mingjue’s severed head. Once Jin Guangyao smuggled it out of Koi Tower, he had probably buried it right here.

Wei Wuxian nodded, then turned back to Nie Huaisang. "Sect Leader Nie, do you have any idea what was originally resting in this coffin?"

Nie Huaisang widened his eyes in utter innocence. "How on earth would I know that? But judging by how San-ge... sorry, Sect Leader Jin looked, it must've been something really important to him."
